issues.description: Metadata CheckID and directory name disagree with code's class name, breaking discovery.
issues.detail: The PR description, CHANGELOG, directory, and metadata.json all use `compute_instance_single_network_interface`, while the docstring and `_test.py` import path are consistent — but the PR title and description reference `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces`. The author cannot state which name is canonical. This is UNREASONED: a check whose own identity is ambiguous cannot have a precondition.

issues.description: GKE exception is a SMUGGLED-GOTO via string-prefix heuristic on instance.name.
issues.detail: The decision to emit MANUAL versus FAIL is taken on `instance.name.startswith("gke-")`. A user-named VM `gke-bastion` becomes MANUAL; a real GKE node renamed by tooling becomes FAIL. The predicate is unrelated to the property being checked (managed-by-GKE). Either query the `goog-gke-node` label / managed-instance-group ancestry, or drop the special case and document it in Notes.

issues.description: Postcondition for the zero-interface branch is incoherent: status remains PASS.
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, `report.status` is left as the initial `PASS` while `status_extended` says the instance has no network interfaces. A VM with zero NICs is not a single-NIC VM; the postcondition `status == PASS ⇒ exactly one interface` is violated. Either raise an explicit error state or treat as MANUAL; do not silently pass.

issues.description: TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the zero-NIC and unnamed-NIC paths have no test coverage.
issues.detail: Tests cover one, two, three, four NICs, and the GKE prefix. The zero-NIC branch — the one whose semantics are wrong — is untested, as is a NIC whose `name` field is absent (defaulted to empty string in `_get_instances`). Coverage by example is not proof, but the absence here means the bug above shipped uncaught.

issues.description: Mutable default `[]` on Pydantic field is fragile; prefer `Field(default_factory=list)`.
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` follows the file's existing style, so this is consistent, but the pattern is a known footgun if anyone later mutates the default. The repo's existing models share this defect; flagging for awareness, not blocking.

issues.description: `interface_names` joining trusts NIC `name`; empty strings produce ugly output.
issues.detail: If the API omits `name`, `_get_instances` defaults it to `""`, then `status_extended` reports `"VM Instance X has 2 network interfaces: , ."` This is cosmetic but indicates the author did not reason about the frame of `interface.get("name", "")`. Substitute a placeholder like `nic[0]`, `nic[1]` by index when name is empty.

review.summary: The check is TESTED-NOT-PROVED and partially UNREASONED. Its identity is ambiguous (PR title says "multiple_network_interfaces", everything else says "single_network_interface"), its GKE carve-out is a SMUGGLED-GOTO via `name.startswith("gke-")` instead of the actual managed-by-GKE property, and its zero-NIC branch silently returns PASS in violation of the implied postcondition. The tests exercise the happy paths the author imagined; the broken branch and the unnamed-NIC case are untested. The structured-programming verdict: REFUSED until the author states precondition, postcondition, and the actual definition of "GKE-managed".
